claim: Likelihood-informed posterior subspaces are established prior art, rather than a new P3-L decomposition.
evidence: Abstract identifies a subspace from relative prior/likelihood influence over posterior support.
limitation: Does not establish actual P1 strong marginal or posterior quality.

claim: Joint parameter/state reduction with a retained prior complement predates P3-L.
evidence: Abstract constructs parameter and state subspaces, approximating posterior by a reduced likelihood factor and marginal prior on the complement.
study_context: Atmospheric integral-equation and groundwater PDE examples.
limitation: An approximate likelihood/prior complement is not an exact strong conditional posterior integral.

claim: Task posterior mean approximation judged by Bayes risk is established in linear Gaussian inverse problems.
evidence: Abstract states low-rank QoI mean approximation optimal under weighted Bayes risk and goal-oriented covariance approximation.
study_context: Linear Gaussian model; QoI, heat-transfer example.
limitation: Cannot transfer its optimality theorem to nonlinear saturating P1 decoder or guarantee pointwise GT gains.

claim: Certified posterior reduction requires distributional derivative information and functional inequalities.
evidence: Abstract gives a KL upper bound using logarithmic Sobolev inequalities, requiring a second moment of log-likelihood gradients and sample-error analysis.
limitation: Contradicts any claim that an anchor spectrum alone certifies dropped-coordinate posterior error.

claim: Derivative-informed surrogates, geometry, DA correction and total training cost are already combined.
evidence: Sections 2.8,4.3,5 and Appendix C cover surrogate-driven geometric proposals, exact full-misfit second stage, training PDE costs, and the relation of misfit-error differences to second-stage ratio.
limitation: Not Maxwell and not an enclosing same-uniform evaluator certificate. Reported speedups do not transfer to TM24.

claim: Goal-oriented ROM potential/gradient errors and induced posterior/transport errors are mature prior art.
evidence: Abstract analyzes reduced-basis potential and gradient errors, induced posterior KL error, and sample errors in Stein variational transport.
study_context: PDE-constrained Bayesian inverse problems with adaptive goal-oriented reduction.
limitation: SVGD approximation guarantees do not certify a particular Full-MH path or actual P1 risk gain.

claim: Pseudo-marginal methods can preserve the ideal marginal target; arbitrary noisy marginal MH need not.
evidence: Abstract distinguishes algorithms sharing ideal marginal stationary law from an obvious inexact Monte Carlo marginal approximation.
limitation: Precise weight positivity/current-randomness conditions require theorem-level reading, not proved from abstract here.

claim: Tallis canonical truncated-normal-moment reference resolves, but its theorem was not retrieved in this run.
evidence: Canonical title, G.M. Tallis,1961,DOI verified; publisher withheld abstract and browser could not access DOI.
confidence: high identity, no substantive evidence tier
limitation: No theorem-level support assigned to P1 saturation recurrence from metadata alone.

claim: Casella-Robert canonical Rao-Blackwell paper resolves, but its contents were unavailable.
evidence: Title, G.Casella/C.Robert,1996,DOI verified; abstract elided and primary browser access failed.
limitation: Cannot claim universal MCMC asymptotic-variance improvement or exact P1 decoder formula from this retrieval.

claim: Tierney-Kadane canonical posterior moments/marginal density reference resolves; content gap remains.
evidence: Title, L.Tierney/J.Kadane,1986,DOI verified; publisher abstract elided and DOI browser returned403.
study_context: Posterior moment and marginal density approximation.
